item.text: Vou seguir o fluxo da skill de engenharia 3D para explicar como começar no CAD3D, sem criar ou alterar arquivos. Também vou destacar as verificações de encaixe, resistência e impressão que importam para um suporte removível em FDM.

---
name: 3d-engineering
description: >-
  Engineer parametric mechanical parts and assemblies with the CAD3D platform. Use
  for product design, enclosures, supports, mechanisms, interfaces, fluid paths,
  build123d/OCP, STEP/STL, FDM/DFAM, and OrcaSlicer workflows. Do not use for
  unrelated software tasks or general 3D art.

# CAD3D product engineering

Use the existing global `cad3d` CLI; it runs the CAD engine (`build123d`/OCP) and,
optionally, the isolated OrcaSlicer manufacturing engine. Do not install CAD Python
packages on the host. Start with `cad3d --help` and `cad3d doctor` when needed.

## Workflow

For consequential products, proceed in gates: requirements → functional architecture
→ mechanical architecture → parametric geometry → system review → manufacturing.
Use `cad3d architecture init --level product` and edit `.cad3d/engineering.yaml`;
validate with `cad3d architecture validate`. Do not create functional solids before
the first three gates pass. Simple spacers/supports may use the lightweight project
level; match process depth to risk.

Model from explicit datums, units, interfaces and parameters. Map each component to a
function, positioning relation and retention method; explicitly declare intended free
parts. Validate geometry and assemblies using `cad3d build`, then run
`cad3d architecture validate --geometry`, `cad3d review`, and
`cad3d report --requirements`. Correct FAIL results and rerun the relevant checks.
PASS requires traceable evidence; declaration or a generated solid alone is not proof.
Treat WARNING and NOT_EVALUATED as unresolved review items. A CAD-valid assembly is
not thereby mechanically stable, printable, physically validated, or ready to release.

Generate technical views with `cad3d render --view engineering`: opaque isometric,
orthographic top/front/side, section, exploded, plus configured hidden-component and
critical-interface views. Review the actual images for occlusion and legibility.
Export with `cad3d export`. For FDM use the versioned printer/material/process
profiles and `cad3d slice --printer elegoo-cc2 --material petg`; inspect
`cad3d slice-report`. Slicing is an estimate, not printer compatibility or physical
validation. Never start a print or transmit a file to a printer.

## Load references by project class

- General product phases and gates: [product_engineering.md](references/product_engineering.md)
- Requirements, YAML contract, interfaces and evidence: [requirements_and_interfaces.md](references/requirements_and_interfaces.md)
- Assemblies, retention, fit and service: [mechanical_assemblies.md](references/mechanical_assemblies.md)
- FDM design and profiles: [dfam.md](references/dfam.md)
- Passive channels and fluid paths: [fluid_systems.md](references/fluid_systems.md)
- Adversarial/system review: [design_review.md](references/design_review.md)
- Professional view generation: [visual_validation.md](references/visual_validation.md)
- Commercial part envelopes: [commercial_components.md](references/commercial_components.md)
- Existing CAD checks: [assembly-validation.md](references/assembly-validation.md)
- OrcaSlicer engine and its limits: [orcaslicer-engine.md](references/orcaslicer-engine.md)

Choose relevant references; do not load every topic for a simple part. Keep requirement
implementation distinct from verification, engineering judgment distinct from automated
checks, and physical validation distinct from CAD/slicer evidence. For adversarial review,
use a fresh Codex context when available. A sequential checklist is not an independent
review; report that limitation explicitly.

usage: cad3d {doctor|init <project>|build|validate|render|export|report|test|architecture|review|calibration|slicer|slice|slice-report} [options]

init creates a project template in a new or existing directory without replacing files.
architecture init|validate and review manage the product engineering contract and review.
CAD commands run in cad3d-engineering Docker. `slicer` and `slice` run the separate cad3d-orca container.

# Mechanical assemblies

Each component has stable ID, function and positioned geometry. Each movable or removable component needs a relation and retention method, or an explicit reason for intentional freedom. Placement only proves location. Distinguish contact, clearance and positive-volume interference. Declared contact does not authorize volume overlap.

Describe interfaces with mating regions/faces, datums, insertion axis, fit/tolerance profile, and intended service operation. Check collision and clearance, then test sampled linear assembly/removal trajectories where supported. Sampling cannot prove continuous collision-free motion or load capacity. For screws, snaps, captured rails and pressure fits, review actual load path, access, deformation and release strategy. Record assembly steps and evidence; unresolved force, fatigue and print anisotropy remain warnings or not evaluated.
# FDM and DFAM

Use declared printer, nozzle, material and process profiles. Treat uncalibrated values as starting estimates, never universal tolerances. Check per-axis build envelope for candidate orientations, wall features, disconnected bodies, overhang/support heuristics, interface orientation relative to layers and slicer estimates. These are assessments, not print guarantees. Choose orientation with explicit tradeoffs; fastest is not necessarily strongest.

Use calibration specimens for clearance, pins/holes, walls, sliding fits, bridges and overhangs. Record measured results against exact printer/nozzle/material/process profile revision. Do not silently propagate a calibration to old project contracts. After printing, record dimensions and physical fit results separately.

item.text:
Para um suporte simples e removível, eu começaria pelo projeto **lightweight**. Se o suporte sustentar uma carga relevante, tiver várias peças ou exigir uma avaliação mais formal, use o fluxo **product** e passe pelos requisitos e pela arquitetura antes de criar sólidos.

**Antes de modelar**, anote: o que o suporte segura e quanto pesa; onde e como ele se fixa; por onde entra e sai; como fica retido e como é solto; e qual impressora, material e orientação de impressão você pretende usar. Defina datums, unidades, interfaces e parâmetros principais, como espessura, folga e posição dos encaixes.

Com esses dados, os comandos principais são:

```sh
cad3d doctor
cad3d init ./suporte-removivel
cd ./suporte-removivel

# Para suporte simples:
cad3d architecture init --level lightweight

# Para um produto com várias peças ou maior risco:
cad3d architecture init --level product
# Preencha .cad3d/engineering.yaml e valide os requisitos:
cad3d architecture validate

# Depois de definir a geometria e a montagem:
cad3d build
cad3d validate
cad3d architecture validate --geometry
cad3d review
cad3d report --requirements

# Inspecione vistas técnicas e estime a impressão:
cad3d render --view engineering
cad3d slice --printer elegoo-cc2 --material petg
cad3d slice-report
```

**Verificações importantes:**

- **Remoção e retenção:** confira a direção de inserção e retirada, colisões no percurso, acesso para soltar e o método de retenção. O suporte precisa continuar preso sob a carga prevista e poder ser removido sem dano.
- **Encaixe:** defina regiões de contato, folgas e tolerâncias. Não trate sobreposição de volume como contato válido. Faça corpos de calibração para medir folgas e encaixes na sua impressora, material e processo.
- **Resistência:** confira o caminho da carga, espessuras e concentração de tensão. A orientação das camadas pode mudar bastante a resistência; a geometria CAD, sozinha, não comprova a capacidade mecânica.
- **Impressão:** verifique envelope por eixo, paredes, pontes, balanços e necessidade de suporte para as orientações candidatas. Confira se a interface removível está orientada de forma adequada em relação às camadas.
- **Evidência:** trate avisos e itens `NOT_EVALUATED` como questões em aberto. Depois da impressão, registre medidas e resultados de encaixe separadamente. O fatiamento é uma estimativa, não uma validação física.

Consulte `cad3d --help` para a lista de comandos; a CLI disponível também oferece `cad3d export` quando estiver pronto para exportar o modelo. Não criei arquivos.
